messages:
maya: Drafting the RN for 0.9.3-canary. Posting a concise blurb + recommended ops language. Need sign-off on rollback wording and pin guidance. Link: https://redwood.internal/releases/0.9.3 :eyes:
chris: Got it. Can you include the exact services we'll pin and the temporary capacity bump details? ops wants the phrasing explicit for SRE runbooks.
sasha: +1 on explicit pins. Suggest we add a one-sentence tl;dr for non-technical folks.
maya: adding both. Proposed snippets below (feel free to copy/edit).
maya: ```
Release notes (public-facing):
- Version: 0.9.3-canary
- Highlights: Improved prefix caching for multi-turn chat; reduced P99 latency by ~8% on long-context workloads.
- Impact: No customer-facing breaking changes. Expected smoother interactive experiences and lower token costs on heavy chat paths.

Internal ops blurb (for status channels & ops runbook):
- Deploy window: 2026-05-14 02:00-03:00 UTC (soft window, will monitor).
- Pinned components: runtime-service@v3.2.1, kvcache-proxy@v1.7.0, model-variant: gptx-q8-v2 (pinned for canary traffic).
- Capacity: +15% reserved burst on dedicated pools during canary (auto scale set).
- Rollback trigger: sustained error rate > 1.5% for 15m or P95 latency regressions > 20% vs baseline.
- Rollback action: immediate pin back to runtime-service@v3.1.9 and model-variant: gptx-q8-v1, route 100% traffic to fallback region us-west-2 for 30m.
```
priya: This reads well. Can we make the rollback action explicit about the deploy-bot command and who executes it?
alex: ops-runbook-bot has a snippet we can paste to ensure standardized wording.
ops-runbook-bot: ```
If rollback required:
1) Trigger deploy-bot rollback: `/deploy rollback --release 0.9.3-canary --to runtime-service@v3.1.9 --model gptx-q8-v1` (ops oncall or release owner).
2) Re-route traffic: `route-manager pin --region us-west-2 --percent 100` (SRE).
3) Post incident summary in #incidents and tag @oncall.
4) Hold change window for 30 minutes to observe.
```
chris: Perfect — include that exact block in the internal announce. Also add a one-liner for executives: "No expected customer impact; rolling canary with strict rollback conditions."
sasha: For the public RN, swap the phrase "reduced P99 latency" to "lower P99 latency" — marketing prefers simpler phrasing.
maya: updated both. New copy below.
maya: ```
Public RN short:
- 0.9.3-canary: Lower P99 latency for long-context chat and improved prefix caching. No breaking changes.
Internal announce (Slack snippet):
Hey team :wave: we're rolling 0.9.3-canary during the 02:00 UTC change window tomorrow. Key points:
• Pinned runtime-service@v3.2.1 and gptx-q8-v2 for canary.
• +15% burst reserved for the canary.
• Rollback triggers: >1.5% errors for 15m or P95 latency +20%.
If rollback is needed, run the deploy-bot rollback command below and notify #incidents.
```
maya: final question — should we call out the config flag we toggled for KV cache TTL? It's low-level but might help debugging.
priya: call it out in ops note only: `kvcache.ttl.override=true (30s)`. Don't include in public RN.
chris: agree. Add the config line and a quick pointer to the perf dashboard (internal).
maya: adding link to dashboard: https://dash.internal.redwood/boards/latency/0.9.3
deploy-bot: Deploy queued: release=0.9.3-canary, env=staging->canary, initiator=maya, queued_at=2360001150. ETA start 2026-05-14T02:00:00Z.
maya: Thanks — I'll post the internal announce in #eng-releases and ping oncall 15m before start.
sasha: I'll take watch for the first 30m. priya will handle rollback if needed.
priya: standing by.
chris: Looks good. Approving RN and internal copy. :thumbsup:
maya: Awesome. Final internal announce draft I'll post in ~10 and then pin the RN in the release board.
ops-runbook-bot: Reminder: tag format for incidents is `INC-<YYYYMMDD>-<short>` — please include when you create the post.
maya: noted, will use INC-20260514-canary.
deploy-bot: Deploy started: 0.9.3-canary -> canary (job id: 98821). Logs: https://ci.internal.redwood/jobs/98821/logs
maya: posting now.
chris: :rocket:
